$comment: How the one link sign-in engine reads a service's start and poll, on both hosts, and the requests it makes: test/link-login.test.js walks it through src/host/link-sign-in.js and LinkSignInRecordTest through LinkSignIn.kt. A case names a service in contracts/link-logins.json, or one of declarations.json's. Every rule of the design's *The dialects* holds for every service: a code of 1 to 16 letters, digits, `-` and single spaces; an expiry of 10 seconds to an hour; a credential of 8 to 4,096 printable ASCII characters; an interval clamped to 2 to 60 seconds, and widened by a `slower` answer (`widen`) within the same clamp; a QR off the visit site replaced by the visit address. `about` says where a body came from.

requests.why: plex.tv's start carries the host's own identifier and product, never a plugin's
the poll names the pin the start answered
the discovery alone carries the account credential, in the service's account header
what the start answered is percent-encoded into the poll's URL
a form body is written as declared, a registered client id as the literal it is, and the engine sets its Content-Type
RFC 8628's poll is a form body naming the device code, every character but letters, digits and *-._ escaped, and nothing in its URL
a credential header's value is its template with the credential in it, whatever characters the credential carries
a JSON body is an object of the filled-in strings, and the engine sets its Content-Type over any spelling of one the service names
what the start answered is escaped as JSON in a JSON body, and nothing else is
plex.tv asks a typed address who it is with a GET that says it reads JSON, and nothing of the service's own headers
an address written with colons is bracketed
another service asks with the method and headers it declares
and with the method it declares, no headers at all included
